I found a valid spill set with total cost 14, but I did not prove it is the minimum, so a cheaper solution may exist.

**Approach.** Two 5-cliques force spills. Nodes {2,5,13,15,18} form a K5 and nodes {0,12,13,22,24} form a K5, so at least one node from each must be spilled. That gives a lower bound of 5 + 4 = 9. The cheapest choices from those cliques (18 or 15, and 24 or 22) did not give a colouring on their own. I tried many spill sets by hand and each failed on forced colourings, including {18,24,10}, {18,22,3} and {15,24,10}.

**Spill set.** I spilled nodes 3, 10, 18 and 24, with costs 2 + 3 + 5 + 4 = 14. After removing them, the colouring below was built by forced assignments. I then checked every edge touching a kept node and found no conflict.

**Re-adding spilled nodes.** Node 10 cannot return, because its neighbours 2, 5, 11 and 15 already use all four colours. Node 3 cannot return either, because nodes 6 and 25 are adjacent and both must take colour 0 or 1, while node 3 would be forced to colour 1.

{"spilled": [3, 10, 18, 24], "coloring": {"0": 2, "1": 2, "2": 0, "4": 2, "5": 1, "6": 1, "7": 0, "8": 1, "9": 3, "11": 3, "12": 1, "13": 3, "14": 2, "15": 2, "16": 1, "17": 0, "19": 3, "20": 1, "21": 3, "22": 0, "23": 1, "25": 0}}
